## Open

### F-165 — tableOptions implied resource: true from any edges binding

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · open_

resource was computed as spec.resource === true || edges.length > 0, so declaring edges on a table
silently switched on the resource-backed name machinery: edit then treats Name as virtual (stripping
it from the UPDATE and renaming core_resource.resourceName instead). Party tables have real name
columns and needed edges, which would have broken party edits. Decoupled to spec.resource === true
and added resource: {nameColumn} for tables whose real display column is not Name. Only access.role
declared edges before, and it set resource: true explicitly, so nothing changed for it.

### F-166 — Loader crashed on any module without a default export (no realm would load)

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Watch.load read module.default and passed it straight to \_validateAndSetHandlerName, so a plain
shared module inside a handler folder (realm/blong-access/adapter/db/account.ts, accessModel.ts,
oidc.ts) threw TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading name) at startup. No realm
could be loaded and no test in the repo could run - it predates this work and came from the
core-split commit. Fixed by skipping such modules (returning an identity transformer), which is the
documented behaviour. Note the same pattern logs an ERROR line per file, which is noisy for an
expected case.

### F-173 — Deleting an ACL-guarded record must release its rules first

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · open_

access_acl keeps FKs to core_resource on principalId/actionId/targetId, but the generic remove
deleted only detail rows, graph edges, the entity row and the resource. Deleting a role that owned a
rule therefore threw AFTER the access_role row was gone, leaving a resource-only ghost; because
core.resource.ensure matches by name and then skips the entity insert, that role could never be
created again under the same name - the matrix spec silently stopped working. remove now deletes the
rules naming the record before touching anything (aclReleaseResource, guarded by acl mode !== none).

### F-194 — Suite children never recorded their realm url, so every named realm loaded twice

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The framework's frameworkRealms dedupe compares a resolved specifier against loadedRealmUrls, which
the wrapper around a suite's children filled from the value those children return. A child answers
with the realm _factory_ (a function), not the module namespace and not the module, so url was never
a string and nothing was ever recorded: every realm a suite named was loaded a second time by the
framework's own list. The visible damage was not the double handlers but the ordering: the second
blong-server copy registered server.subject.validation AFTER the realm's explicit gateway overrides
(access.access.validation), so Registry.\_validations() replaced the override and eight blong-access
Playwright specs failed with 'must have required properties capabilityId/roleId/userId' - the ids
those overrides exist to make optional. Found by printing what the wrapper sees, after reasoning
about URL equality and pnpm symlinks led nowhere. Fix: record the url inside loadRealm, where the
module exists, into a Set carried on the shared api so every nested load writes into the tree's one
set. Lesson: when a dedupe silently does nothing, print the value the comparison is made of - and
check the _registration order_ consequence, because a duplicated realm does not fail loudly, it
reorders.

### F-195 — A shared module that imports node:async_hooks kills the browser bundle

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The new callTrace.ts imported AsyncLocalStorage from node:async*hooks at module scope. Vite resolves
that to a browser-external stub that throws on the named export, and callTrace is reached from the
\_shared* realm machinery (semanticContext, BrowserLog), so every browser suite in blong-access died
at load with 'does not provide an export named AsyncLocalStorage' - the spec failed immediately
after I had verified the server side. The framework already documents the pattern for exactly this
(semanticContext.ts attaches the emitter vocabulary instead of importing it); the file to check
before adding a Node-only import to anything reachable from load.ts is whether the _browser_
platform reaches it. Fix: callTrace.ts holds a CallTraceStorage handed in by attachCallTraceStorage,
and callTraceNode.ts (imported from the Node-only Log/SemanticLog init) attaches the real
AsyncLocalStorage. Consequence to remember: in a page there is no scope, so callsEnabled() is false
and a browser records no calls at all - which is the right default there anyway.

### F-197 — A shared-graph module must not import semantic-log values

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The browser bundle broke a second time, now from the refactor. callTrace.ts - reached by
semanticContext, which the browser loads - imported callPhaseMessage from the capability subpath,
whose module graph reaches Node's async_hooks; Vite resolved it to a browser-external stub and every
browser suite died at load, exactly as when callTrace.ts had imported AsyncLocalStorage directly.
The rule is sharper than the earlier version: a module on the shared path may import semantic-log
types (erased at runtime) and may reach behaviour only through the vocabulary the server bootstrap
attaches; anything else it needs has to be handed to it, which is why CallEvent now carries the line
the channel built. Checked before running this time: the only remaining value imports of
semantic-log in blong-gogo are Gateway.ts (server-only, behind vite-ignore) and the two log
implementations.

### F-198 — Two invariant tests of the target package decided the shape of the move

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Moving the logger's lifecycle into semantic-log took two rewrites of the same file: the first draft
_extended_ the new base and the framework never instantiated it (load.ts identifies components by
'prototype instanceof Internal'), and the second had the emitter-side base import the service, which
test/emitter-entry.test.ts forbids even as a type. Both were discoverable before writing: the
package has emitter-entry, offline and parity tests that state exactly which modules each half may
reach, and the consumer's loader states how it detects a component. Lesson: read a package's
invariant tests and the consumer's loader before moving code across a half boundary, and prefer
options over inheritance when the consumer's base class is not yours.

### F-214 — The test-group flow observed nothing

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Watch.start minted a flow around the dispatch that builds a test group's steps, then ran the steps
after runInFlow had returned - so the scenario's calls were made in no flow at all and /flows listed
nothing for a test group while every step passed. The flow now wraps the dispatch and the chain
together. Cost: the symptom ('tests pass, no flow observed') is indistinguishable from a realm with
no test groups, and it took a probe in Watch/AdapterBase to find, because the flow identity is only
visible on the records.

### F-215 — A rule restored in one package and left broken in the other

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The caller of an edge is the leg id's first half - restored in core/semantic-log so the ledger and
the diagram read it there - and that alone changed nothing that a reader could see: the framework
kept DECLARING legs the old way, with a port id as the caller half (`login.loginDispatch`, `srv.db`)
and a handler name as the method half (`accessPermissionList`). A leg id is read by its two halves,
so a rule about what they mean is only half a fix if the site that mints them is not changed with
it: the leg has to be `<caller namespace>.<wire method>`, which meant the port's `config.namespace`
rather than its id, and `methodParts(name)` rather than the name the handler was written under.
Symptom while only the library half was done: the diagram still drew every arrow from one
participant, and derived participants from handler names (`accessPermissionList`,
`meterLimitMeter`). Lesson: when a rule about an identifier moves, grep for the code that MINTS the
identifier, in every package, before believing the rule is in force.

### F-261 — The codec login helper yields nothing outside the codec namespace

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The codec realm's `testLoginTokenCreate` helper is the framework's own way to open a scenario with a
login, and it does not work from a suite whose scenarios live outside the codec namespace: the step
it returns calls `loginTokenCreate`, which resolves in the port of the namespace the step runs in,
so the call goes nowhere and the step yields nothing.

Nothing reports that. The helper's own subtest passes in under a millisecond, because the handler
that returns the chain is trivially fine; the nested login step is what fails, and a caller that
awaits it waits forever instead of failing (see the hang entry in core/blong-chain). The suite that
hits this learns it only by tracing which requests the adapter actually sent.

The demo now writes its own login step, which is three lines and reported properly. Worth
considering: the helper should either dispatch the login where the caller's namespace can reach it,
or refuse when it cannot, rather than yielding a silent nothing.

### F-275 — A static chain import broke the page in the dev server only

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The gateway realm's Playwright run failed with a SyntaxError that named only Vite's stub — it said a
browser-external module `does not provide an export named 'EventEmitter'` — and seven of its tests
failed because the login screen never rendered. Watch.ts had begun importing chain.ts for a value,
and the loader reaches Watch.ts through a dynamic import it executes at startup, so that value
import pulled @feasibleone/blong-chain and its named `node:events` import into the graph a dev
server links before any code runs. The same edge is harmless in a bundle build, which stubs the
builtin and leaves TestExecutor without a base, so no CI job could see it, and the bundle guard
cannot either, because Watch.ts is not in the built graph. Lesson: when an error names a stub rather
than the importer, list the modules the dev server actually requests — a Playwright request listener
plus a grep of the served text is enough — and remember that a production bundle is far more
forgiving than the dev loader. The same class of failure is recorded as F-195 for node:async_hooks
in a shared module; what differs here is that only the dev server failed, and that the bundle guard
could not see the module at all.

### F-279 — A tap-only package had no CI report because its entry had to remember an intent

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Only the entries that passed `ci` in CI wrote Allure results, because `watch.allure.enabled` is off
by default and the `ci` block is what turns it on. Every package whose only runner is tap and whose
entry named the intent (kukum, handler-test-poc) or did not (blong-eip, blong-cucumber,
blong-sim-api, blong-sim-tcp, config-hot-reload, test/framework) therefore landed in the CI
summary's Report column as `—`, and `collectPublishable` had no `publish/` directory to link because
there were no results to publish. Fix: `activeConfigs` adds the `ci` intent when `isCI()`, so the
captured-run block applies to every module whatever the entry asked for — which also activates the
db adapter's own `ci` block (keep-alive plus retry) in CI, where the packages that needed it most
were the ones not asking. Verified on `demo/blong-eip`, `blong-cucumber`, `blong-sim-api`,
`blong-sim-tcp`, `config-hot-reload` (each now writes `allure-results-tap` and publishes), and on
`realm/blong-commander` that two producers still merge into one report. What made this cost time:
the cell is `—` both for a package that produced no report and for one that produced none because
nothing asked for one, the CI's `.ci-report` directories are not published so the reason is
invisible from outside, and the site lists only packages that published — so the only way through
was to reason from `collectPublishable`, then reproduce each package locally under `CI=1`.

### F-347 — A custom handler needs a validation to be reachable, and a three-word name

> _2026-10-04 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Calling a new party read through the browser backend answered 404 Not Found twice before it worked.
A method is reachable over RPC when its table is declared in the realm schema (the generic CRUD) or
when a gateway validation file declares it; a handler of its own without one is simply not routed.
Once declared, the name mattered: methodParts in core/blong-gogo/src/lib.ts splits the leading word
group only, so a four-word handler name glues its fourth word onto the predicate -
partyAclFixtureGet became party.acl.fixtureGet. Renaming the file to partyFixtureGet fixed it. Both
failures read like a missing handler rather than a naming or exposure rule, which is why the work
took two cycles.

### F-351 — A declared expect was stripped by the JSON-RPC body schema

> _2026-10-04 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Making the party suite's expected refusals quiet took six runs and a temporary console.error in the
gateway, because the feature looked implemented and did nothing. The route's body schema listed
jsonrpc, id, method and params only, so validation removed expect before the route read
request.body.expect; the configuration flag was on, the client was sending the field, and the route
simply never saw it. The diagnostic that settled it printed the keys of request.body at the route,
which is the check to reach for first: when a body field seems ignored, look at the schema before
anywhere else. Instrumenting the gateway is faster than reading the transport chain, which was the
wrong place to look for two runs.

### F-352 — An untyped error cannot be declared expected

> _2026-10-04 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The RBAC refusal was built as a plain Error with statusCode 403, so isExpectedError (which matches
on error.type) could never demote it and a test could not describe the refusal it was probing. Every
expected-error declaration therefore depends on the failing side being typed, and the message has to
stay stable while the type is added, since the browser and playwright tests match Authorization
denied in a string.

### F-356 — The ACL SQL builder threw for a table with no scope edges

> _2026-10-04 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Trying to declare a guard for a table with acl: {mode: 'explicit'} and no scopes of its own made
aclCheckSql throw 'ACL SQL placeholder mismatch: 14 placeholders, 16 bindings' before any verdict,
so the read failed as a 500 rather than being refused. The cause is the branch it falls into when
there is no scope set: the SQL inlines the record column a correlated list filter passes, and the
bindings still added options.recordId on top. Nothing covers that shape because every other guarded
table in the repository declares scopes or selfScope, so the branch is reached by tests only. Fixed
by binding the record id only when there is a placeholder to bind, and pinned in
core/blong-gogo/src/acl.test.ts, which is the file's only unit test: the integration suites cannot
tell a mismatched bind list from a refusal.

### F-360 — bin/blong.ts passes a relative run target unresolved

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

core/blong-gogo/bin/blong.ts passes the run target through unresolved, so a relative target such as
./index.ts is imported relative to runServer.ts and fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for
core/blong-gogo/src/index.ts. The watch wrapper bin/blong-watch.ts resolves the target first, so the
same invocation works there. Use an absolute target for a one-shot run, or make bin/blong.ts resolve
like the wrapper.

### F-361 — a custom top-level layer folder is silently never loaded

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

discoverLayerFolders in core/blong-gogo/src/load.ts iterates only WELL_KNOWN_LAYERS, and a folder
the framework does not know is reachable only as a child realm (a folder with its own server.ts),
never as a layer. realm/blong-kustomize had a k8s/ folder with layer.server.ts plus a port and
handlers; nothing loaded and no error was reported, only the missing effect. Fix: put the layer in a
well-known folder and gate it with layer.server.ts, or make the folder a child realm with server.ts.

### F-366 — The k8s adapter had no batch API, so a generated Job could not be applied

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

getApiForResource covered core, apps, networking and rbac only, so a Job or CronJob fell through to
the core API and would have been sent to a method that does not exist. The generator emits a seed
Job for the shared SuiteVolume backend, so the gap was one step from becoming a runtime failure.
Added batchV1Api plus the job and cronjob resource names. The same check is worth running before
assuming any generated kind can be applied.

### F-368 — assert.matchSnapshot throws though the type declares it

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Writing the first golden test took three runs for two separate reasons. IAssert in
core/blong/types.ts declares both snapshot() and matchSnapshot(), but matchSnapshot throws Cannot
read private member from an object whose class did not declare it, because only snapshot() is bound
by the test executor; the working call is assert.snapshot(value, name), as the framework's own
core/blong-chain tests use. The second reason is that tap refuses to create a baseline implicitly:
the first run fails with Snapshot file not found unless TAP_SNAPSHOT=1 is set, which is correct
behaviour but worth knowing before assuming the test is wrong.

### F-369 — The k8s adapter missed every compound kind's method name

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

getMethodName built the client method by capitalising the first letter of the resource type, which
yields createTokenreview and createNamespacedDaemonset where the generated client has
createTokenReview and createNamespacedDaemonSet. The lookup is a typeof function check inside
callApi, so a miss throws Invalid Kubernetes Operation without naming either the method or the kind,
and nothing in the message points at the resource. Found because a live TokenReview failed while the
same call to a one-word resource worked. The blast radius was larger than the new code:
persistentvolumeclaim, daemonset, statefulset, replicaset, networkpolicy, rolebinding, clusterrole
and clusterrolebinding were all unreachable, which means the operator apply path added in Phase 10b
could never have created a DaemonSet or a PVC — the two kinds the nodeLocal and shared volume
backends respectively need. Fixed with a METHOD_RESOURCE map; the lesson is that a name-derivation
helper whose only failure mode is a generic runtime error has to be exercised once per kind.

### F-375 — A relative target is accepted and then crashes the framework import

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

bin/blong.ts decides whether the first positional is a target with existsSync(resolve(maybeTarget))
and then hands the unresolved string to autoRun, so runTarget calls import(target) with whatever was
written. A relative target passes that check yet resolves against runServer.ts rather than the
working directory, and the process dies on ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND with a path inside the framework,
which reads as a packaging fault rather than an argument one: the container that passed
./suite/suite/blong-suite/index.ts from a working directory that contained it looked correct and
could not start. Deployers must therefore write the entry as an absolute path. The framework should
resolve the target before importing it, which is a one-line change in the same place the check
already resolves it to test for existence.

### F-378 — A deployed monolith needs two settings before it can start

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

A suite deployed into a cluster dies twice before it serves anything, and both symptoms name nothing
about the cause. First the framework resolves a service id as a local port, so the pod asks for the
hostname rpc-subject and dies on ENOTFOUND: the fix is resolution.impl kubernetes, which maps each
internal rpc name to the Service the generated tree creates. Then the process dispatches a startup
call to a namespace it serves itself over the network and is refused, because the resolver names a
Service with no ready endpoint yet and the server is not listening: the fix is remote.canSkipSocket
true, which is what the browser platform and the integration intent already set. Both are suite
config, and the second is only correct for a monolith profile, so a suite that deploys itself has to
know its own deployment shape.

### F-380 — A generic error wrapper hid the API message twice

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The cluster adapter answered k8s.generic Kubernetes Error with no detail for a custom-resource read,
and the cause took a debug run and a probe to rule out. The same shape cost the earlier deployment
exercise its diagnosis: a refusal is only useful when it carries what the API said, and the adapter
has one path where it does and this one where it wraps everything the same way. What the wrapper
hides is which call failed and why, so the first thing to fix is the error, not the call it was
about.

### F-382 — The patch content type belongs to the generated client, not the caller

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

A status write against a CRD came back as HTTP 400 'error decoding patch: cannot unmarshal object
into Go value of type []handlers.jsonPatchOp', because the generated client picks the first media
type it supports from its own list — json-patch, merge-patch, apply-patch — and that list starts at
json-patch. Neither an options.headers entry nor the older strategic-merge header changes it; the
parameter the old client honoured is ignored by this one, in silence. The body therefore has to be a
JSON patch for a custom resource, and the lesson is to read the generated method before guessing
which header wins.

### F-402 — The k8s adapter read the wrong field for an error status

> _2026-10-06 · core/blong-gogo · open_

k8s.ts mapped API failures with k8sError.response?.statusCode, but @kubernetes/client-node 1.4.0
rejects with an ApiException carrying {code, body, headers} and no response at all - verified with a
three-line probe against the live client. Every 404, 401, 403 and 409 therefore reached callers as
k8s.failed with status none, and the four typed errors the map declares were dead code. The visible
cost was an apply that treated any read failure as absence: the second reconcile pass over an
existing object created it again, answered 409 already exists, and reported an object that was there
all along as a failed step with a message naming the create rather than the read (F-404). Lesson:
when error handling branches on a library's error shape, print the shape once instead of trusting
the version's documentation.

### F-409 — node-gyp downloads headers the image already has, and stalls

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The image build hung for twelve minutes with no progress at all: 2.4 GB written into the pnpm store,
the node-rdkafka install running node-gyp rebuild, node-gyp blocked on a socket with no children and
write counters frozen. node-rdkafka vendors its librdkafka, so the only thing left to fetch was the
Node headers, which node-gyp downloads from nodejs.org unless it is told otherwise. The image has
them: the node base image ships 64 headers at /usr/local/include/node, and node-gyp reads
npm_config_nodedir. Two things made this expensive to diagnose: a stalled download looks exactly
like a slow one from the outside, and the build had been started in a terminal that was recycled, so
its own log was gone and the only evidence was the process table and the io counters. Fixed with ENV
npm_config_nodedir=/usr/local before the install step. The interrupted first build still produced a
tagged image, because pnpm carries on when a package install script dies - so the tag is not
evidence that the native addon was built, and the image has to be checked for it rather than
trusted.

### F-412 — A manifest-only image layer misses file: dependencies and rush.json comments

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · open_

So the generator that writes the block (core/blong-gogo/docker/manifests.mjs, --write and --check)
also walks each package.json's file: specs and emits a copy for each target directory. The lesson
generalises: the set of files an install reads is not the set a lockfile names, and a fast failure
is worth more than a slow one — the two failures here cost under a minute each because they happened
before the native build.

### F-421 — A folder a realm names as a child is skipped by layer discovery

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The well-known layer table activates a folder only when discovery reaches it, and discovery skips
every folder the realm already lists in children. A realm that named orchestrator and gateway as
children therefore had to repeat them under each intent in its own config, because the table's k8s
column could never apply; removing the per-intent lists alone took the realm out of the generated
suite tree, since the plan attributes a namespace through the ports a realm contributes. The fix is
to name no children for folders the table knows, and the check is a fresh generation diffed against
the deployed tree.

### F-426 — A destructuring read hid the second consumer of config.public

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Concluding that `config.public` had one reader cost a wrong plan item and a correction after the
fact. The grep was for `\.public` over three directories, and it cannot see a destructuring read:
`realm/blong-login/orchestrator/login/token.ts` takes the pair as
`const {public: keys} = gateway?.config?.()`, a second and load-bearing consumer that would have
broken if the copy had been deleted outright. The path list was the second error — the accessor's
declared shape is a type in `core/blong/types.ts`, outside the three paths. Lesson: when the claim
is "nothing else reads this", search the property name on its own, whole tree, excluding only build
output, and include the packages that consume the accessor rather than only the one that defines it.
Here the shape had to survive even though the storage could go, which is the difference the missed
reader would have hidden.

### F-379 — A dockerignore is not a gitignore, and the bare fix for it was not one either

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The image build copies the repository's folders, so the context is whatever `.dockerignore` lets
through, and the file was written the gitignore way: bare names like `.vscode-test`, `node_modules`,
`.tap` and `coverage`. Podman does not read them that way. A pattern without a slash is matched
against the context root only — verified by building a scratch context whose `.dockerignore` held
the bare name `.vscode-test` and watching the nested `ext/rest-fs/.vscode-test` arrive in the image
anyway. So the first fix for this did nothing: `ext/rest-fs/.vscode-test` (fifteen downloaded VS
Code builds, about 15 GB), every package's `node_modules` (9.1 GB), `.tap` (2.0 GB) and `coverage`
(2.2 GB) all reached the builder, and each build left a 22 to 27 GB intermediate image behind as a
dangling one — three of them were sitting in the store, about 110 GB. Measured with a walker that
applies buildah's semantics: the context went from 19.6 GiB to 0.3 GiB once the entries carried a
`**/` prefix, with no other change. Lesson: a bare pattern in `.dockerignore` means the root entry;
write `**/name`, and prove an ignore file with a scratch context rather than by reading it.

### F-372 — Error parameters need the params wrapper, and the adapter does not use it

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

A parameterized error renders its placeholders as question marks unless the values arrive as params,
so `errors['x']({reason: 'y'})` prints 'could not be verified: ?reason?' while
`errors['x']({params: {reason: 'y'}})` prints the reason. The realm's login learned this the hard
way, and the k8s adapter still calls its own errors the flat way, which is why messages like Missing
key value for a key have always read as placeholders. The adapter's API-error path now uses the
wrapper, and the rest of its calls are recorded as a follow-up.

### F-358 — resource: true names cannot be filtered, only matched

> _2026-10-04 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The unguarded case needed a table whose records could be identified by name, and two candidates
failed in ways worth remembering. core.resource has no model, so declaring it in meta/db/db.ts
creates the table but not the API and every call answers 404 Not Found. access.capability and
access.acl have models, but their names live in core_resource.resourceName and are attached after
the query: the access realm's own Browse page searches description for exactly that reason, so
filterBy on capabilityName or targetName returns nothing. The way through is to read the rows and
match the joined display name in code, which is what the matrix target's nameColumn does. The model,
not the schema declaration, is what exposes the CRUD over RPC.

## Resolved

### F-094 — Knex `table.list` prefixed table names with the subject twice

> _2026-08-23 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

`access.{tableName}.find` with `tableName='access_user'` built `access_access_user`, and the list
also returned junk `$subject_*` tables and every visible schema's tables. The fix filters to the
connected database plus `{subject}_%` and the junk names, and strips the `{subject}_` prefix so
`{tableName}` is the object name.

### F-095 — tap's order-sensitive snapshots broke on an appended `id` field

> _2026-08-23 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The mongodb adapter's `{...doc, id}` appended `id` at the END of the document, so a manually
inserted `id` right after `_id` failed tap's order-sensitive snapshot compare. Regenerate with
`TAP_SNAPSHOT=1` and then revert the unrelated snapshots, because the regeneration reformats ALL of
them.

### F-096 — A realm's async child loads only when its config block exists

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

A child declared as a function or async import
(`async function core() { return import('@feasibleone/blong-core/server.ts') }`) is NOT loaded
unless the realm config has a matching block for the child's name (`mergedConfig[itemName]`). The
symptom was `objectSchema` keys lacking the child (`['mysql']` only) and core tables never syncing.

Adding `core: {}` (or per-intent blocks) to the realm `config` fixed it. Cost ~28 minutes in the
blong-int-adapter mysql round and was root-caused by reading `core/blong-gogo/src/load.ts`.

### F-097 — Generic knex `add` returned an empty row for an explicit binary PK

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The `add` case fell back to `inserted[0]`, whose auto-increment `insertId` is 0 for a
non-auto-increment PK, so a row added with an explicitly supplied `ulid`/`uuid` PK came back empty.
Prefer `insertCols[keyName]` (the explicit PK) before `inserted[0]`.

### F-098 — `prepareResultRow` mutates the row and masked a binary PK

> _2026-08-19 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

In the generic knex exec `get` case, `masterKey = row?.[keyName]` was read AFTER
`prepareResultRow(row, binaryCols, table)`, which converts Buffer to base64 in place (documented
behaviour), so `Buffer.isBuffer(masterKey)` was false and the declared graph-edge attachment block
was silently skipped. Several debug runs did not spot it because the raw row (pre-mutation) IS a
Buffer and direct knex reproductions return Buffers — only the mutation ordering differed.

Capture `masterKey` from the raw `row` BEFORE calling the helper: never read the PK off a row after
passing it to a mutating 'prepare' helper, or have the helper return a copy. The technique that
worked was printing `JSON.stringify(row, (k, v) => Buffer.isBuffer(v) ? 'BUFFER:' + v.length : v)`
right after `query.first()` and again after `prepareResultRow`.

### F-100 — `blong --help` crashed instead of printing usage

> _2026-08-19 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The `blong` and `blong-watch` CLIs now short-circuit `--help`/`-h` and print usage with exit 0
before realm-create and `autoRun`, through the shared helper `core/blong-gogo/src/cliHelp.ts`, so
help works from any directory. The sibling `blong-dev` CLI also prints usage and exits 0 on
`--help`/`-h`/`help`; its usage list used to appear only through the unknown-command branch, which
exited 1.

### F-101 — The dev database had no documented name and was never created

> _2026-08-19 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The knex adapter auto-creates a missing database in `start()` when `knex.createDatabase: true` (the
default in the `dev` intent through the shared `srv.db` adapter; opt out with
`srv.db.dev.knex.createDatabase: false`). The dev naming pattern is documented in the blong-schema
skill and derived automatically by `blong-dev sql`, so nobody has to iterate to find the name.
`ensureDatabase` in `core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/schema/knex/database.ts` is covered by unit tests
with an injected connection.

### F-102 — The knex retry recursed because the wrapped `then` was called again

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Verifying the intermittent `PROTOCOL_CONNECTION_LOST` behaviour in CI meant reading knex/tarn
internals: `QueryBuilder.clone()` builds a fresh builder from its `_*` fields and does NOT copy
own-property `then`/`insert`/`update` overrides (which makes it safe for retry re-execution), and
`then()` re-runs from builder state on each call. The first retry implementation recursively called
the wrapped `then` on the first attempt, because `builder.then` had just been overridden, and died
with 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'.

Capture `originalThen` before overriding and use it for attempt 0; use the clone's own prototype
`then` for retries.

### F-128 — MCP over Streamable HTTP took four attempts because every failure is a 500

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Sharing one stateless transport across requests made the second request fail, because the SDK
expects a per-request transport in stateless mode. Switching to per-request servers made
`tools/list` return `Method not found`, because the protocol requires `initialize` on the same
session and a fresh server has not been initialized. The working shape is the documented stateful
one: one `McpServer` plus one transport per `Mcp-Session-Id`.

Even then the tool list was empty, because `Mcp.init()` read `gateway.describe()` during load —
routes are published in `registry.start()`, so the read has to happen inside the fastify plugin
factory, which runs at `gateway.start()`.

`reply.hijack()` plus a transport that writes its own response hides every error as an empty 500:
wrap the call and log, and read the route table only after start.

### F-129 — Anchoring a caller's regex with `$` turned a pattern list into an exact match

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

`Mcp.routes()` appended `$` to each configured regex to 'anchor' it, so the default pattern
`^kukum\.` became `^kukum\.$` and matched nothing: the MCP endpoint answered `initialize` but
advertised zero tools. Do not normalize regexes the caller supplied.

### F-137 — An intent's config lost to a later `default` block

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The `cli` intent's `gateway: false` and `rpcServer: false` had no effect: `blong cli` still logged
`Server listening at http://127.0.0.1:…` and `gateway listening at random port …`. Two
investigations went nowhere first — a grep found no `port: 0` anywhere, `ut-function.merge` handles
`false` correctly, and `ConfigRuntime.mergeConfigs` showed `loaded.gateway=undefined` (blong-config
contributes nothing, and `~/.blong_devrc` explains only the `watch.logLevel` that did apply).

The truth came from printing the `configs` array itself: the standalone-realm wrapper declares
`rpcServer: {port: 0}` and `gateway: {port: hasBrowser ? 8080 : 0}` in its `default` block, and that
block is pushed after the framework's intent blocks, so it wins. When an intent's config does not
take effect, check the order of the `loadedConfigs.push(...)` calls and not only the merge function:
`default` is not a low-precedence name, it is whichever `default` block is pushed last.

### F-138 — A green test suite proves nothing about types

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Adding the `cli` intent and the `exit` config key cost three extra debug cycles, all of them purely
about types: `tap` transpiles TypeScript without typechecking, so a suite could be fully green (261
passing) while `blong-dev lint` reported 3–4 `tsc` errors. The intent tables in
`core/blong-gogo/src/load.ts` are literals typed against `IBaseConfig` and `IActivationConfig`,
which had never been exercised with a new intent name or an unknown key — `IActivationConfig<T>`
enumerated only the five built-in names, and `IBaseConfig` is `additionalProperties: false`.

Run `blong-dev lint` in `core/blong-gogo` after touching anything in `load.ts` or `types.ts`; a
green `blong-dev test` proves nothing about compilation. A second trap lives in the same area:
`TOptional<T>` makes a key optional at the top level of a `TObject` shape but not inside a nested
`TObject` shape, where keys resolve as required — which is why `watch: {enabled: false}` failed to
type-check however the inner keys were annotated. Prefer a permissive `TObject` for config bags such
as `watch`.

### F-139 — A server-only `process.env` read in a shared module broke the browser

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Adding `exit: Boolean(process.env.CI)` to `load.ts` made the whole Playwright leg fail: every
browser test timed out at 30 s and the suite took 410 s instead of 21 s. `load.ts` is shared by both
platforms — Vite serves the same file to the browser — and `process` does not exist there, so the
realm never finished loading: `ReferenceError: process is not defined at loadRealm`.

Before using `process`, `fs`, `os` or any Node builtin in `load.ts`, or in anything else the browser
bundle reaches, ask which platforms import it. Route it through an optional chain
(`globalThis.process?.env?.['X']`) and put it in a function rather than a module constant, so tests
that set `process.env.X` at runtime still work. Grep for existing uses first: `runServer.ts`,
`loadServer.ts`, `Gateway.ts` and `RestFs.ts` are server-only, which is why they were fine and this
was not.

### F-140 — A 'verified (do not re-derive)' note about `this` was an inference

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

A plan carried a 'Verified mechanics (do not re-derive)' section asserting that `this` inside a
`library()` function is the port, so `this.platform` and `this.registry` would work 'with no
framework change'. It was derived from reading `layerProxy.ts:68-83` and seeing
`fn.apply(port, params)` — but that call sits behind a `??`, so it only runs in the not-yet-attached
fallback path. For a normally attached library function the proxy returns the raw function, and
`this` is the lib object.

An inferred mechanic labeled 'verified' is still an inference. The probe that settled it was a
temporary `library()` file whose handler threw `JSON.stringify(...)` of what `this` was, so the
value surfaced through the gateway's error message. Do that whenever a plan decision rests on a
claim about `this`, `arguments`, proxy behavior or load order, because the happy path is exactly
where reading gives the wrong answer. The probe also showed the fix was small — putting `platform`
and `registry` onto `lib` — rather than the design change the wrong note implied.

### F-141 — Every realm folder needs a `package.json` beside its entry

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

`Cannot find module './package.json'` from a realm's `server.ts` has nothing to do with the imports
in that file: the loader reads a `package.json` beside the realm entry, so every realm folder needs
one. The error names the consumer, not the missing convention — `blong-eip` carries
`eip/package.json` for exactly this reason.

### F-142 — A per-intent activation block with a different shape needs a generic

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

A per-intent activation block whose shape differs from `default` fails to type-check unless the
orchestrator is given a generic (`orchestrator<Record<string, unknown>>(…)`), and the error does not
point at the cause. `blong-kukum` needed the same annotation.

### F-143 — `--output` defaults on `isTTY`, so a piped child gets JSON

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The CLI's `--output` defaults on `process.stdout.isTTY` (`core/blong-gogo/src/cli.ts`), so a piped
child receives JSON where a terminal receives text. Tests that spawn the CLI must name the format
explicitly; the mismatch cost one debugging cycle.

### F-144 — Component logs go to fd 1 directly, so redirecting stdout misses them

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Pino writes component logs to file descriptor 1 directly rather than through `process.stdout.write`,
so the CLI's stdout redirect does not catch them and they land in the result. Configuration, not
redirection, is what quiets them.

### F-220 — A declared call nobody recorded is only ever seen from the callee's side

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Declaring the dispatch orchestrator's hop (declareCall) made the ledger aware of the leg only
through the callee's receipt: the diagram drew 'received, no caller was observed' instead of the
arrow, because a leg is evidence only when a record is written inside it and the dispatcher's own
port record is written before the leg is declared. Declaring and recording are one act in the
handler proxy (declareCall around recordedCall); a caller that declares without recording buys a leg
nobody can see. Lesson: when adding a declaration to a new call path, check what record that path
writes inside the scope - the framework's tracing is the proxy's, not the ports'.

Fixed: the dispatch orchestrator records its hop through the call channel inside the leg it declares
(D-239, D-240). The gateway realm's observed flow now draws gateway->>db with its answer.

### F-259 — A login failure threw the encrypted envelope, not the reason

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The MLE adapter hooks for the login endpoints delegated errors to the base receive with the body
still encrypted, so a failed login threw the ciphertext envelope and the server's actual error - a
404 for the access realm port, in the case that surfaced it - was unreadable to the caller that has
to act on it. Fixed in the same session: loginTokenCreateResponseReceive,
loginTokenRefreshResponseReceive and loginTokenRestoreResponseReceive now decrypt the error before
delegating, which is what the adapter receive does for every other response. Verified against the
demo: the failure reads Request failed with status code 404 (Not Found): POST
.../rpc/ports/access/request.

Fixed in this session and verified against the demo run: the failure now reads Request failed with
status code 404 (Not Found): POST .../rpc/ports/access/request.

### F-269 — Realm start and tap both pause for seconds before their first line

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Root cause found. The delay is the log cache in `~/.blong/log-cache`, not the loader.

Measured on this machine, the same command and the same tree: the realm reaches its first log line
at 9.0 s with the cache present and at 0.67 s with the cache directory moved away. A tap run in
`realm/blong-access` used to stay silent for about 36 s after `TAP version 14` and `1..1`; with an
empty cache the framework logs at 3.8 s and there is no gap at all. `cacache.ls` on the directory
takes 10,001 entries and 8,500 ms, and that call is the `loadIndexes` at open in
`core/semantic-log/src/cache.ts`, so every process pays it before its first line.

What is wrong with the directory. It holds 451,436 files under `index-v5` and 420,150 under
`content-v2` (1.9 GB), while only 10,001 entries are live (5,000 records, 5,000 payloads, the
marker), so the bound in `cache.ts` itself works. A sample of 3,000 index files ends with a
tombstone line in 2,930 of them: pruning calls `cacache.rm.entry(dir, id)`, which appends an
`integrity: null` line and leaves the file in place. Since a `cacache` key is hashed into its own
index file, the directory grows by one file per record ever written whatever the bound does, and
`ls` reads every one of them. `cacache.rm.entry(dir, id, {removeFully: true})` deletes the file.

Compaction is the other half. `cacache.verify` is what compacts the index and reclaims orphaned
content, and its only online caller is the sweep in `maintainOnOpen`, gated behind the
`__blong_retention_state__` marker once a day. The pino transport in
`core/blong-gogo/src/pino-cacache.ts` writes the same marker, and its own prune does not compact, so
either writer can refresh the marker and starve the other's compaction. That is how 441k dead index
files and 410k orphaned content files accumulated.

The lesson: a content-addressed store with a per-write bound still has to delete its index files,
and an "already swept" marker shared by several writers only works when every writer does the same
work.

Fixed: retention deleted the index file of a pruned entry (removeFully) and a bloated directory is
reclaimed when it is opened. Realm start 9.0s to 1.25s; the tap gap is gone.

### F-272 — A literal dynamic import bundled the Allure integration into browser builds

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The three lazy imports of `@feasibleone/blong-allure` in `src/chain.ts` were written as literal
specifiers — `await import('@feasibleone/blong-allure')` — which the bundler resolves however
dynamic the import looks, so the whole node-only integration was in every browser build: 785 modules
whose module graph carried `blong-allure` with `node:fs`, `node:fs/promises`, `node:crypto`,
`node:url` and `node:child_process`. `core/blong-browser/src/browserBundle.test.ts` was failing on
exactly that list, under a name that did not say which package was at fault. Fixed by assembling the
specifier at runtime (`allurePackage()`), the trick `load.ts` already uses for the server half of
the platform map, and by adding `blong-allure` to that test's server-only list so the same
regression is reported by name rather than as a pile of builtins. Lesson: a `@vite-ignore` comment
does not stop the bundler resolving a specifier — only a specifier it cannot evaluate does — and any
node-only import from browser-reachable code should be checked with that bundle test before it is
believed.

Fixed in the same change: chain.ts imports the package through a runtime-assembled specifier
(allurePackage), and browserBundle.test.ts now lists blong-allure as server-only so the regression
fails by name. The browser bundle test passes with the package absent from the graph (785 modules
before, 766 after).

### F-299 — The CLI host could not create a nested or existing folder

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Scaffolding more than one file into one folder through the kukum CLI failed: a missing parent was
refused, and a folder that already existed was an error, because IPlatformApi.mkdirSync was bound
straight to the node:fs mkdirSync, which is neither recursive nor idempotent. engine.apply calls it
as a make-sure-the-parent-exists before every write, so the contract callers expect is recursive and
idempotent; loadServer now passes a wrapper that calls mkdirSync with recursive true. Any future
call site should assume that contract.

Fixed: loadServer.ts now passes a wrapper that calls node:fs mkdirSync with recursive true, so the
parent is created and an existing folder is a no-op.

### F-370 — A CLI config override for a component key is dropped in silence

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Running the k8s intent with a command-line override for the output directory wrote its 22 files to
the default system/kustomize instead, and nothing in the output said the override had been ignored:
the log line reports the directory it actually used, which is the only reason the mistake was
visible. Declaring the key in the port's own validation, with additionalProperties true, did not
change it, so the drop happens before the component sees the config or the key path is not the one
the CLI builds. Worth finding out, because a silently ignored override is the kind of thing a
deployment would do once and believe.

Root cause found: the port was addressed at the realm level (`--kustomize.outputDir`) while the
framework builds a port config from `mergedConfig[realm][port]`, and a key outside that slice is
dropped in silence — no validation error and no log line. Documented the path, declared the slice,
and recorded the missing warning as a todo in `core/blong-gogo`.

### F-373 — The framework Dockerfile cannot be built with podman

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The realm runbook tells a reader to bring an image in with podman because docker is absent on this
machine and the k3d nodes are podman containers, and podman refuses the Dockerfile at its first real
step: COPY --parents is a BuildKit feature, so the build dies with COPY only supports the
--chmod --chown and --from flags. The deployment run needed a stand-in image built from the deploy
folder instead. A plain COPY per category folder plus the existing .dockerignore is portable to both
and needs no rush install at that step.

Closed by removing the BuildKit-only syntax rather than by giving up podman: the Dockerfile now
copies one folder per package category (rush.json plus common, core, realm, test, suite, demo,
tools, docs, ext) instead of one COPY per package.json with --parents, and the release stage copies
the whole deploy folder with the prune done by the builder (rm -rf .rush, find -type d -name
docker -o -name rush-logs) instead of --exclude. podman 4.9.3 built the image: 1.1 GB, imported into
both k3d nodes with ctr.

### F-413 — A release default resolved Services the tree never writes

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

And the Services the tree writes are named after realms: access, core, db, login, marine and
web-http, none of them a namespace. A process calling another namespace asks for the namespace name,
so the tree owes a Service per namespace the plan recorded, selecting the deployment that serves it.
The realm-named ones stay, because they are what the gateway port and the front-end ingress expose
(D-430). Where the deployment stands: the image and both artifacts are rebuilt and re-seeded, the
database block names host db and the credentials, and the tree regenerates with four deployments
whose args are release plus their own layer flags — but the pods still crash on this resolution, so
the live login proof is blocked here.

The tree writes a Service per namespace the plan recorded (subject among them) and the realm-named
ones stay for the gateway port and the ingress; the released process that asked for rpc-subject now
resolves.

### F-423 — A write-back through the config proxy made a path its own value

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Resolving the pair by reading gateway.sign through mergedConfig and writing the result back crashed
the CLI with RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded inside ConfigRuntime. The proxy returns a
path proxy for any object read, so writing that value back made the path contain a proxy of itself
and the next read recursed. The lesson: on this proxy, read from configRuntime.rawSnapshot and write
only fresh values, since writing is delegated to the same backing object the proxy reads.

The resolution reads configRuntime.rawSnapshot instead, so the trap is no longer on the path; the
rule is recorded in D-442.

### F-427 — An unnecessary mle change, from reading a transport error as a key error

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

An unnecessary change to `mle.ts` and `Gateway.ts` — removing the stored `config.public` and
deriving it in the route and in `Gateway.config()` — was made because a 400 from the login endpoint
carried jose's `Key must be one of type CryptoKey, KeyObject, or JSON Web Key` and read as a
key-configuration failure. It was not: that endpoint expects an MLE-encrypted request, and the plain
JSON the e2e script sends cannot satisfy it, so the same 400 comes back from a correct deployment.
The user spotted this and asked for the change to be reviewed. The review's evidence is a cluster
run of the unchanged code: `blong-dev proxy` in front of `svc/login`, then the same POST through the
proxy answers 200 with an `access_token` and no private member, while with the change deployed that
answer carried `d` for both halves, because the login then read the config's own pair instead of
public-only material. Two lessons. A jose key error can come from a malformed request rather than
from the process's keys, so reproduce through the transport the route expects before touching key
handling. And a refactor of "repetition" in a security-shaped path needs the exposure question asked
first: this one replaced a correct arrangement with a leak, and only the test added afterwards would
have caught it.

resolved: the change was reverted, the unchanged framework logs in through an MLE client and answers
no private member, and the leak guards are now in place.

### F-431 — Ignoring the envelope members left an empty meta printed

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

The header lifts `$meta.mtid` and `$meta.method` onto the line, and the detail beneath it printed
both a second time, so the transport ignored the two keys. That cannot work: pino-pretty deletes the
_leaf_, so an envelope that held only those two members was left as `{"$meta":{}}` on every
framework record — one stray key became another. The printer now rewrites each line on the way in:
the two members move to a key the header reads and the detail ignores, and the record keeps
everything else the envelope carried. The trap worth remembering is the order inside pino-pretty:
`messageFormat` runs on the _unfiltered_ log and the filter runs after, so a rewrite that removes
the members before the formatter also removes them from the header — the first attempt did exactly
that and the header lost the two words it exists to print.

fixed in this change

### F-429 — A part of a handler name could not be more than one word

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Writing a compound kind readably was impossible: `methodParts` splits camelCase, so
`clusterPersistentVolumeClaimApply` became `cluster.persistent.volumeClaimApply` and the k8s adapter
read a middle word that named no API (F-379). The workaround was a lump plus a `METHOD_RESOURCE`
table gluing it back into the client spelling, which is a naming rule that only splits and cannot
represent the shape a caller wants to write. The fix is a separator that joins: an underscore or a
hyphen glues the word after it to the one before, so `clusterPersistent_Volume_ClaimApply` is
`cluster.persistent_volume_claim.apply`, the separator stays in the name because it is the only
record of where the words are, and the adapter joins them again. A splitter used as a naming
convention needs a join, or every multi-word concept pays a table.

fixed in this change

### F-438 — A relative CLI target was found in cwd and imported beside runServer.ts

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-gogo · resolved_

Running `blong ./index.ts k8s` from a suite folder failed with
`Cannot find module core/blong-gogo/src/index.ts`, a path the caller never typed: bin/blong.ts
accepts the first positional as an optional target when `existsSync(resolve(target))` says it
exists, which resolves against `process.cwd()`, but autoRun handed that bare `./index.ts` straight
to `await import(target)`, and a relative specifier resolves against the importing module —
runServer.ts — not the working directory. The detection and the load disagreed about the base, so a
file that was just shown to exist was reported missing. Fixed by resolving the target against cwd in
autoRun before runTarget, which is what the fallback path (resolve(cwd, 'index.ts')) and the e2e
script (an absolute path made by cd && pwd) already did.

autoRun now resolves the target against cwd before runTarget imports it, and src/runServer.test.ts
covers it: a relative target that exists resolves and reaches the module (the assertion is the
missing-default-export message, which is only reachable once the path resolved), where before it
reported a file under core/blong-gogo/src that nobody had named.
